goals: PRIMARY (requested): project change in recharge in the Naches by ~2050 under a warming scenario
FALLBACK (feasible): characterize baseline (1980-2018) recharge and its soil/elevation spatial variability
SENSITIVITY (conditional): quantify recharge response to imposed warming perturbations, if forcing perturbation is enabled

model_choice.rationale: ELM resolves the full water balance including snow, ET, and sub-surface drainage (recharge proxy QDRAI) in a single column; spatial sampling spans watershed heterogeneity. But the requested future projection depends on forcing the stack does not have.

answerable: baseline (1980-2018) recharge magnitude and its variability across dominant soils
relative recharge sensitivity to imposed warming ONLY IF a forcing-perturbation capability is added

not_answerable.aspect: projection of recharge to ~2050 under a warming scenario
not_answerable.why: only historical forcing (1980-2018) is available; there is no future scenario forcing and no delta/bias-correction pathway to build one
not_answerable.needs: future-scenario forcing ingest (RCP/SSP or delta-perturbed forcing generator)

not_answerable.aspect: elevation/climate control on recharge (rain-snow transition, snowmelt timing)
not_answerable.why: single-column forcing is not elevation-downscaled, so columns at different elevations differ only by soil, not by temperature/precip-phase — the snow-driven mechanism cannot be isolated

not_answerable.aspect: validation of simulated recharge/snow against measurements
not_answerable.needs: observation-dataset ingest (SNOTEL SWE, streamflow baseflow, or recharge estimates)

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band x dominant soil) — for the FEASIBLE baseline characterization only
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands x up to 3 dominant soils = up to 9 strata; ~12 columns spans the populated strata with light replication in the rain-snow transition band where recharge is most sensitive. NOTE: elevation bands here index landscape position/soil context, NOT a resolved climate gradient (forcing is uniform) — see feasibility.not_answerable.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: concentrate columns in the mid-elevation rain-snow transition where snowmelt-driven recharge is largest and most sensitive; sample valley bottoms (thickest soils, focused recharge) and uplands for the storage endpoints. Downstream expander samples real DEM/soil rasters within the bbox.
sampling_strategy.replication: light (1 extra column) in the rain-snow transition band to capture soil variability where the recharge signal concentrates

sampling_plan.reason: zone of largest and most sensitive snowmelt-driven recharge; oversampled across soil classes to resolve infiltration-vs-drainage partitioning
thick soils and focused recharge endpoints; spans dominant soil textures at the low-elevation water-balance limit
snow-storage endpoint controlling melt volume and timing that feeds downslope recharge

validation_design.comparison: none — GAP: no co-located or analog recharge observations provided

validation_design.observation_source: SNOTEL (not ingested; would be analog/co-located if added)
validation_design.comparison: analog — flagged; requires observation ingest capability before use

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline historical forcing (1980-2018), native gridded soil

requires_capabilities.capability: future-scenario forcing ingest (RCP/SSP or delta-perturbed forcing generator)
requires_capabilities.why: the request is a 2050 projection under warming; only historical forcing exists

requires_capabilities.capability: elevation-downscaled forcing (temperature lapse + precip-phase by elevation)
requires_capabilities.why: recharge here is snow-controlled; uniform forcing cannot represent the elevation/climate gradient
requires_capabilities.blocks: attributing recharge change to climate/snow; isolating elevation control

requires_capabilities.capability: snow/SWE diagnostic output and melt-timing metrics
requires_capabilities.why: recharge response to warming operates through snowpack and melt timing
requires_capabilities.blocks: mechanistic interpretation of any recharge change
any validation of baseline or perturbed recharge

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up to equilibrate soil moisture / deep drainage
requires_capabilities.why: recharge/QDRAI depends on equilibrated storage state

assumptions: Recharge is represented by ELM sub-surface drainage (QDRAI); deep percolation below the soil column is not separately resolved.
The Naches is snowmelt-influenced, so the recharge climate signal is dominated by snow processes.
Dominant soil classes will be resolved by the downstream expander from gridded soil rasters (not provided here).
The elevation bands index landscape/soil context only; with uniform forcing they do NOT encode a climate gradient.
open_questions: Which warming scenario/target (e.g. +2 C, specific SSP, delta vs dynamically downscaled) does the user intend for 2050?
Is a delta-perturbation of historical forcing (temperature offset + precip scaling) an acceptable surrogate, or is full scenario forcing required?
Are any SNOTEL / streamflow / recharge observations available to ingest for validation?
Is 'recharge' defined as sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) or net percolation past a specific depth?
